text: Three tricycles are parked outside a nursery. How many wheels altogether?
Odd one out: Tuesday, Thursday, March, Saturday.
why: March is a month; the rest are days.

text: Grandma knits 3 scarves a week. How many has she made after 4 weeks?
A cricket side of 11 has lost 4 wickets. How many of its batters are not yet out?
why: 11 − 4 = 7, counting the two at the crease.

text: In a bakery queue, Ellie is 5th from the front and 5th from the back. How many people are queuing?
why: 4 ahead of her, 4 behind her, plus Ellie.

text: Spot the number that isn't prime: 2, 3, 5, 9, 11.
A lift takes at most 8 people. What's the fewest trips needed to carry 30 people up?
why: Three trips carry 24; the last 6 need a fourth.

text: How many sides do a hexagon and an octagon have between them?
A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 run off. How many does he still have?
A rope ladder hangs over a moored ship's side, with 4 rungs above the water. The tide rises a metre. How many rungs are above water now?
why: The ship floats up with the tide, and the ladder with it.
